# Ambri's Furrow — Colchis

> **Enemy:** the Grand Harness, the Father of Devis and the Legions of Hell · **Hero:** Eristavi Zurab Bronze-Arm · **Scenarios:** 5

In the spring of 1914 the Grand Harness moved — straight toward Ambri's grave. The Colchian levy stands in the same furrow that Ambri's foot ploughed: their grandfathers dug it out, their fathers died in it. Now Zurab Bronze-Arm's warband must not let the city reach the grave.

## Sacrifice: Beka the Ox-Driver (1872)

**"The Last Yoke".** On the day of Ambri's burial, as the giant was being lowered into the gate, the Father of Devis thrust his heads up from below and broke the yoke of the steam oxen. The twelfth ox, out of control, turned back from the crater's edge. The ox-driver Beka climbed onto the ox's neck, opened the steam valve by hand and turned the ox back toward Ambri — ox and Beka went down into the Wound together, as Ambri's last load. The gate was sealed. To this day the Colchian ox-drivers count twelve oxen and quietly name a thirteenth — Beka.

## Scenarios

### 1. Night Captives (1914)

Every night the heretics snatch captives in no man's land for the altar. The warriors of a lost outpost are still alive.

- **Objective:** bring 3 captives (markers) tied up in the enemy's half back to your edge; one model leads a captive (−2" movement).
- **Special rule:** Night: visibility 12"; models with torches or night-eyes see at 18".
- **Reward:** each captive brought out: +1 Renown; all three — one free warrior (Levy).

### 2. The Harbour of the Sea Gate (1914)

Gveleshaps and heretic sailors attack the supply harbour to weaken the front with hunger.

- **Objective:** at the end of each round, control more of the 3 piers (objectives) — 1 point; 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** from round 2 the enemy enters from the water's edge (landing).
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch. in supplies.

### 3. Beka's Furrow (1914)

The Grand Harness's forward chains have collapsed the stretch of the Furrow where Beka went down in 1872. The old ones say the front has never fallen here.

- **Objective:** hold the table's centre line (the Furrow) for 6 rounds: each round, if you have more models in the Furrow, 1 point.
- **Special rule:** Beka's memory: your models in the Furrow take Fear tests at +1. Once per battle a fallen model may stay as "the last load": remove it, and every enemy within 3" takes 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown; one warrior in the warband gets the name "Beka's Brother" (+1 Nerve).

### 4. The Second Battle of Dragon's Field (1914)

The Bakbak-Devi is at the head of the Harness again. The Fleece Dragon is far away — now soldiers must break the Harness's chains.

- **Objective:** 4 chain posts at the enemy's edge (objectives, Armour 4, 4 Wounds); destroy 3.
- **Special rule:** posts can only be damaged in melee or by explosives. The enemy may take one tier IV unit outside the budget (Harness guard).
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; the Grand Harness halts for one scenario (in the next battle the enemy gets −50 mch.).

### 5. The Grave's Gate (1914)

The city has reached the grave. The altar's shadow lies across Ambri's barrow. Now or never.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: defend the barrow (table centre, 6") — at the end no enemy model may stand on it.
- **Special rule:** both sides may field a tier V giant (scenario rule). From round 4, each round roll d10: on 1–3 Ambri's voice comes from the barrow — all your models know no fear this round.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every surviving warrior gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The Grand Harness pulled back from the barrow — for the first time since 1904. New names have been added to the Furrow, and on the day of the burial the Colchian levy now falls silent twice: for Ambri and for Beka.

camp:iberia.en:
# The Thunder Mountains — Iberia

> **Enemy:** the spawn of the Father of Devis and the heretics of the Grand Harness · **Hero:** Spasalari Nino Thunder-Eye · **Scenarios:** 5

Iberia's mountain fortresses guard the eastern edge of the Wound. The Grand Harness's march has brought devis into the valleys and cut the thunder-fortresses off from one another. Spasalari Nino's warband must link the fortresses again — before the city reaches the grave.

## Sacrifice: Bacho the Khevsur (1871)

**"The Ninth Day".** In the autumn of 1871, in Qursha's Ravine, one of the Father of Devis's heads came down into the ravine — behind Amirani's back. The Khevsur Bacho stood in the throat of the ravine for nine days with thirty men, with sword and mail shirt, while Amirani fought up ahead. On the tenth day the head broke into the ravine; Bacho bound the fortress's last lightning coil to his shield and walked into the devi's jaws. The head fell in the valley and never grew back. Every autumn the Khevsurs carry Bacho's shield back to the throat of the ravine.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Cut-Off Fortress (1914)

Devi-spawn have besieged a valley fortress; the fortress's lightning coil has gone silent.

- **Objective:** bring one engineer or sapper to the fortress (on the enemy's side) and hold it there for 2 rounds — the coil switches on.
- **Special rule:** the enemy's devi-spawn regrow (Regrowth). Once the coil is on, the fortress fires one thunderbolt each round (Power 4, lightning).
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Border Path (1914)

Tushetian shepherds say the heretics use an old path; the nagazis smell the Listeners' trail.

- **Objective:** 5 path markers on the table; the enemy scout is at one of them (written down secretly). Find and kill it before it reaches your edge.
- **Special rule:** a unit with a nagazi reveals a marker when it comes within 6".
- **Reward:** victory: +1 Renown, and you choose the enemy's deployment in the next battle.

### 3. Bacho's Ravine (1914)

A devi's head is rising in the throat of Qursha's Ravine again — this time led out on the Grand Harness's chain.

- **Objective:** hold the throat of the ravine (12" from your edge) for 6 rounds; the enemy's tier IV "Devi Head" (outside the budget) must be stopped.
- **Special rule:** Bacho's shield: once, one of your shield-bearing models may "bind the coil" — one melee attack at Power 7, lightning; afterwards the model dies.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; the shield-bearer who bound the coil is remembered by name — every shield-bearer in the warband gets +1 Nerve in the next battle.

### 4. The March of the Thunder Fortress (1914)

The Thunder Fortress must leave the valley for the Wound — to block the Grand Harness's road.

- **Objective:** get your tier IV model (or an escort of 3 models) off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** the valley is narrow: the table's central strip is 12" wide, with cliffs on both sides (climbers only).
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.; in the finale your tier IV starts with one extra Wound.

### 5. The Shadow of the Armazi Colossus (1914)

The Grand Harness is touching the eastern edge of the Wound. The Armazi Colossus and Amirani stand on the same side — once again.

- **Objective:** 7 rounds: destroy the head of the Harness chain (objective on the enemy's side, 8 Wounds, Armour 5) or hold your edge to the end.
- **Special rule:** tier V giants are allowed. Devis wounded by lightning cannot regrow that round.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every surviving warrior gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The head of the Harness chain fell into the valley, and the great city could not cross the eastern edge. The fortresses' coils answer one another again — at night the mountains glow with a line of lightning, from fortress to fortress.

camp:hell.en:
# The Planned War — the Legions of Hell

> **Enemy:** Colchis, Iberia and the allies of the Ring · **Hero:** Marquis Sabnock · **Scenarios:** 5

Beelzebub plays the war like chess, and his pieces are the legions. Marquis Sabnock has his orders: before the Grand Harness marches, destroy the light side's fortifications and clear the road. For the legions this is not wrath — it is a plan.

## Sacrifice: Recruit No. 4417 (1907)

**"The Number That Remained".** In 1907, on the night of Beelzebub's arrival, Behemoth broke its chains and trampled through its own camp — toward the flask sheds, where thousands of recruits had not yet been woken. Recruit No. 4417, whom no one had given an order, locked the shed door from the inside, opened the steam boiler's valve and met Behemoth at its feet. The explosion brought the monster to its knees. The legions do not remember numbers — but since then no flask has been given that number.

## Scenarios

### 1. Halphas's Line (1914)

The Legion must build a new line of fortifications in no man's land — before the eyes of the light side.

- **Objective:** in 4 rounds place 3 fortification markers (a garrison-builder or sapper stays still for 1 round) and hold them to the end.
- **Special rule:** Orders: Legion units within 6" of the leader take Fear tests at +1.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Rank.

### 2. Malphas's Night (1914)

The shed of the Colchian steam oxen lies behind the front. It must be destroyed before Ambri's Remembrance Day.

- **Objective:** blow up the shed at the enemy's edge (objective, 10 Wounds, Armour 4).
- **Special rule:** Night: visibility 12". The enemy gets one tier IV "Ox" outside the budget, which wakes from round 3.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Rank; the enemy's next battle is without tier IV.

### 3. The Shed Door (1914)

The light side's raiders attack the flask shed — where No. 4417 once stood.

- **Objective:** hold the shed (6" from your edge) for 6 rounds; for every round it survives, 1 recruit joins your warband (after the battle).
- **Special rule:** The locked door: once, one of your recruits may "let the number remain" — remove it, and every model within 3" (both sides) takes 2 Wounds.
- **Reward:** each round survived — 1 recruit; victory: +2 Rank.

### 4. Andras's Whisper (1914)

The allies of the Ring eye each other with suspicion. Andras's Whisperers are tasked with deepening their discord.

- **Objective:** "set" two of the enemy's allied units (or any two) against each other: Andras's Whisperers use Discord successfully 3 times.
- **Special rule:** on a successful Discord the enemy model does not activate this round. Shooting at the Whisperers is at −1.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Rank; the enemy cannot hire allies in the next battle.

### 5. Before the Harness (1914)

The Grand Harness is nearing the grave. The legions must take the last fortification — exactly according to plan.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: take the enemy's fortification (8" from their edge) and hold it for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** tier V is allowed (Behemoth). From round 5, Beelzebub's order: once per round one of your units activates twice.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; Sabnock is raised from Marquis to Count — every surviving warrior gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The fortification fell according to plan, and Beelzebub moved his piece one square forward. But in the camp the recruits whisper about a number that no one will ever be given — the first whisper in the Legion that Andras did not sow.

camp:harness.en:
# The March of the Harness — the Levy of the Grand Harness

> **Enemy:** Colchis, Iberia and the allies of the Ring · **Hero:** the Harness-Lord · **Scenarios:** 5

The rebels no longer have names — only blood and the Harness. The great city marches toward the grave, and every day the altar needs more. The Harness-Lord's warband must open the road for the Harness. But a rumour runs through the ranks about a woman who took back her name in 1899.

## Sacrifice: Mzia, Who Took Back Her Name (1899)

**"The Chain of the First March".** On the Grand Harness's first march the Bakbak-Devi went berserk and lunged toward the captives' cages — at the bottom of the city, where children lay too. A rebel woman, who had no name then, leapt onto the devi's chain, caught the chain on a wheel and blocked it with her own body. The devi stopped. The city's wheel took her. Since then the heretics whisper that before she died she shouted her name — Mzia — and that a name can be taken back. The priests forbid the story.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Night of Blood (1914)

The altar needs captives. The rebels go out on a night raid into no man's land.

- **Objective:** "take captive" 3 enemy models in melee (when they fall, they count as captives) and bring them to your edge.
- **Special rule:** Night: visibility 12". Heretics have double Rage in round 1.
- **Reward:** each captive: +2 Blood (the altar).

### 2. The Kajis' Workshop (1914)

The kaji smiths need the armour left on the battlefield for new bodies.

- **Objective:** 5 scrap markers on the table; at the end of each round, 1 point for each you control; 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** a kaji smith standing still within 1" of a marker makes it worth two points.
- **Reward:** victory: 1 free Kaji-Stitched.

### 3. Mzia's Chain (1914)

The cages by the Harness's wheel are filling again. One rebel told a child her name — and the priests heard.

- **Objective:** 6 rounds: defend the wheel's chain (8" from your edge) against light-side raiders trying to free the cages.
- **Special rule:** Taking back a name: once, one of your rebels may "chain herself to the chain" — she can no longer move, but knows no fear and has 1 extra Wound. If she is alive at the end of the battle, she leaves the warband — with a name.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Blood. If a name was taken back, your leader gets +1 Nerve (doubt makes the strong stronger).

### 4. The Road to Khvamli (1914)

The chains are on Khvamli, and of the last two hundred no one came back. The Harness-Lord knows the road they took.

- **Objective:** get one scout or leader off the enemy's edge; the enemy must stop you.
- **Special rule:** Mountain path: cliffs in the middle of the table, only two passes. Your warband secretly chooses which pass it uses.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Blood, and in the finale one of your units enters from the enemy's rear.

### 5. On the Grave (1914)

The Grand Harness touches Ambri's barrow. The altar's shadow lies across the grave.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: take the barrow (centre, 6") and stay there for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** tier V is allowed (the Bakbak-Devi). For every fallen captive sacrificed on the barrow, one of your models gets +1 attack this round.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every surviving warrior gets +2 experience.

## Ending

Blood was spilled on the barrow, and the seal cracked — but did not break. The priests say more blood is needed. But among the rebels two stories now go around: one about the altar, the other about the woman who took back her name. And more and more of them listen to the second.

camp:listeners.en:
# Forty Locks — the Brotherhood of Listeners

> **Enemy:** every nation — and the Harness-Lord, who has "left" the Brotherhood · **Hero:** Master Kalistrate · **Scenarios:** 5

In 1914 the Brotherhood's locks are coming undone in every separate war — the nations find them one after another: the nail, the clock, the compass, the lighthouses. Master Kalistrate watches thirty years of work collapse. And the Harness-Lord, an old brother, is taking Ambri's lock for himself. The Brotherhood has one way out: new locks before the old ones are found — and Ambri's seal before the Harness-Lord gets it.

## Sacrifice: Adela the Engineer (1871)

**"Her Own Lock".** On the Night of Opening Adela, a Brotherhood engineer, opened her own lock in the valley's seal — as she had been ordered. Then she saw what came up: a head of the Father of Devis, which chose neither nations nor Brotherhood. Below the valley was a town where her sister lived. Adela went down into the seal and closed the lock by hand — from the inside, while the head was climbing up. The valley's gate shut. The Brotherhood struck her name from its lists. The coalition never learned of it. In the town her sister still believes Adela was a ship's engineer who died at sea.

## Scenarios

### 1. False Rank-and-File (1914)

Post is arriving at a light-side outpost — with drawings of a new lock. It must fall into the Brotherhood's hands.

- **Objective:** get the post marker (on the enemy's side) to your edge.
- **Special rule:** Sleepers: up to 3 of your sleeper models (normally 2). The enemy cannot guard the post marker in round 1 — it doesn't know yet.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Locks.

### 2. The Voice-Master's Night (1914)

Two light-side detachments hold one ford. One false order is enough to make them fire on each other.

- **Objective:** give false orders to two enemy units with your Voice-Masters and survive 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** a successful false order: the enemy unit fires once at its own nearest ally.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Locks and +30 mch.

### 3. Adela's Valley (1914)

The Harness-Lord's people are opening the valley's seal — the one Adela closed. For the first time, the Brotherhood defends a seal.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: defend the seal (centre) against the heretics of the Grand Harness and a devi-spawn (the enemy's IV).
- **Special rule:** Adela's lock: one of your engineers may go down into the seal — it leaves the battle, but the seal can no longer be opened (automatic victory if it reached the centre before round 6).
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Locks; Adela's name quietly returns to the Brotherhood — the leader gets +1 Nerve.

### 4. The Gifted Colossus (1914)

A bronze statue stands in the town square — a gift from the coalition. Tonight it must stand up.

- **Objective:** get the Gifted Colossus (your V) to the town gate (the enemy's edge); the town garrison defends.
- **Special rule:** tier V for you; the enemy gets a IV outside the budget. For the first 2 rounds the garrison thinks the statue is "theirs" — they cannot shoot at it.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Locks.

### 5. Ambri's Lock (1914)

The Grand Harness is on the grave. The Harness-Lord wants Ambri's lock for himself, the Brotherhood — for itself. The light side fights them both.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: take the lock marker (the barrow, centre) and carry it to your edge; the opponent — the Grand Harness or a light faction.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. The sleeper Kalistrate (hero) appears within 6" of the barrow.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The lock is in the Brotherhood's hands — neither the Harness-Lord's nor the nations'. Kalistrate keeps it and waits. They say that in the Brotherhood's old list one name has been written in again, by hand, in the empty space: Adela. Why — no one says.

camp:kajeti.en:
# Ambri's Material — Kajeti

> **Enemy:** everyone — and they sell to everyone · **Hero:** Zarda, Queen of the Kajis · **Scenarios:** 5

Kajeti wants the greatest material in the world: Ambri's body. The kajis do not seek the seal and do not serve gods — they love their craft. For the Grand Harness they forge bodies, for the legions they name a price. In 1914, as everyone heads for the grave, Queen Zarda raises her fortress onto its feet.

## Sacrifice: Varsha, the Old Kaji (1899)

**"The Silver Chain".** On the Grand Harness's first march the Bakbak-Devi broke from its chains and charged the Kajeti forge-wagons — where the kajis' children worked. The old kaji Varsha tipped over the furnace cauldron and poured molten silver over the devi's chains — the chains were welded to the ground, and the devi stopped. The silver poured over Varsha too. Those silver chains hold the devi to this day — and every year Kajeti makes the Grand Harness pay for them. The kajis say Varsha struck a bad bargain: one chain, one life. Yet no one lights her furnace.

## Scenarios

### 1. Battlefield Material (1914)

On Dragon's Field lie old armour and the bones of slain monsters. The kajis want them.

- **Objective:** 5 material markers; at the end of each round, 1 point for each you control; 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Kaji hammer-bearers standing still within 1" of a marker — 2 points.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Silver.

### 2. The Legion's Order (1914)

The Legion has paid Kajeti for new armour. The light side attacks the cargo caravan.

- **Objective:** get the caravan (3 markers) to the enemy's edge (the Legion's depot).
- **Special rule:** riders on forged horses carry a caravan marker +3" further.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch. and +1 Silver.

### 3. Varsha's Furnace (1914)

The Bakbak-Devi is breaking the silver chains. The Kajeti wagons are in its path again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: defend 3 silver chains (objectives, your side); the devi (the enemy's IV, outside the budget) breaks them.
- **Special rule:** Varsha's cauldron: one of your masters or hammer-bearers may tip over the furnace — the devi is welded to the ground for 2 rounds, the model dies. If the devi was stopped, you may "sell" it: the Grand Harness has −50 mch. in the next battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Silver.

### 4. The Fortress on Its Feet (1914)

The Kajeti fortress is standing up. First it must leave the valley — and the valley is guarded by the fortresses of Iberia.

- **Objective:** get the fortress-colossus (your V) out of the valley (the enemy's edge).
- **Special rule:** V for you; the enemy — a IV+ or IV outside the budget. The valley is narrow (12").
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Silver.

### 5. Ambri's Material (1914)

Everyone stands at the grave: the light side, the Grand Harness, the legions. The kajis want just one thing — one piece of Ambri, as material.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: take the shard of the barrow (centre) and carry it to your edge.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Everyone else fights each other: any enemy unit engaged with the second opponent does not shoot at you.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

Kajeti carried off a shard of Ambri — small, the size of a palm. Zarda will not put it in the furnace: she says some material must first be understood. By Varsha's cold furnace the shard grows warm at night. The kajis cannot yet explain it.

camp:ring.en:
# Forty Languages — the Ring Battalion

> **Enemy:** the Grand Harness, the legions and the monsters of every war · **Hero:** Colonel Levan Four-Tongues · **Scenarios:** 5

The Tithe detachments come from forty nations — every year, under the Sea Gate Accord. One battalion, one uniform, forty languages. In 1914, with every nation in its own war, the battalion stands alone on the southern edge of the Wound — and the Grand Harness is coming straight for it.

## Sacrifice: Nora the Interpreter (1888)

**"Eleven Languages".** On a night in 1888 a head of the Father of Devis broke through the battalion's southern trench. The order to fall back was given — in one language. Along the line stood detachments of eleven nations, and they did not understand the order. The interpreter Nora ran along the trench — past the head — shouting the order in every language, from detachment to detachment. Eleven detachments fell back. Nora stayed with the eleventh, where the head came down. Every new interpreter in the battalion is taught her oath: "Everyone must understand the order."

## Scenarios

### 1. The New Tithe (1914)

New detachments have arrived — from three nations, with three languages. The heretics attack that night.

- **Objective:** 6 rounds: hold the trench (12" from your edge); the warband must include units of 3 different allies.
- **Special rule:** Confusion of tongues: without an interpreter, allied units receive the leader's orders only within 3".
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Nora's Trench (1914)

The southern trench is breaking again — in the same place. Again, everyone must understand the order.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: 4 allied units must fall back from the trench (table centre) to your edge before the devi's head (the enemy's IV) crosses the trench.
- **Special rule:** Nora's oath: an interpreter who runs the line (from one side of the table to the other) gives every ally +2" movement this round; she knows no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; every interpreter in the battalion gets +1 Nerve.

### 3. The Ring Train (1914)

An armoured train carries supplies around the Wound. The legions are tearing up the rails.

- **Objective:** get the train (your IV) along the rails to the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** Rails: the train moves +4" only along the centre line; Furrow sappers repair the rails.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 4. The Thirty-Seventh Plate (1914)

The Sea Gate Colossus is missing one plate — a new nation's. It must be brought up from behind the front.

- **Objective:** get the plate marker (on the enemy's side) to your edge; two models carry it.
- **Special rule:** the Listeners' sleepers (the enemy's) appear in your ranks too: the enemy may have 1 sleeper model.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown; in the finale the Colossus has 2 extra Wounds.

### 5. The Southern Edge (1914)

The Grand Harness is coming for the southern edge. The battalion is alone — and holds one line with forty languages.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: hold the line (12" from your edge); at the end no enemy may stand on it.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Tithe: in this scenario up to 75% of the budget may be spent on allies.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The Grand Harness did not cross the southern edge. The battalion still speaks forty languages — and holds one line. On the Sea Gate Colossus there is a new plate, the smallest, with one word, written the same in every language: "Nora".

camp:hellenic.en:
# Typhon's Storm — the Hellenic League

> **Enemy:** Typhon and the spawn of Echidna · **Hero:** Eirini · **Scenarios:** 5

On the shores of the Greeks Typhon's storm never ends, and Talos — Hephaestus's bronze guardian — is the only thing holding back the sea. The engineer Eirini assembles automaton phalanxes, but Talos falters in the middle of battle, and no one can work out why.

## Sacrifice: Niko the Smith's Apprentice (1886)

**"The Storm Wall".** In the storm of 1886 Talos fell on the shore — steam was pouring from its heel valve, and Typhon's serpent legs were already coiling around the harbour. The smith's apprentice Niko crawled to the fallen giant's heel, plugged the valve with his own hand and stayed in the jet of steam until Talos got to its feet and met Typhon in the sea. The steam took Niko. In Hephaestus's forge every repair of Talos begins with his name.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Shore of the Hydras (1914)

Hydra-spawn are attacking a fishing village; for every head cut off, two grow back.

- **Objective:** defend the village's 3 houses (objectives) for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** the enemy's tier IV is a "Hydra": it regrows; if wounded by fire — it doesn't.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Storm Wall (1914)

Typhon's storm stands on the shore like a wall; under the wind the phalanx advances slowly.

- **Objective:** get 2 units off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** Wind: at the start of each round roll d10; on 1–4 the range of all shooting is halved.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Niko's Heel (1914)

Talos falls again — in the same place as in 1886. The heel valve is open.

- **Objective:** the fallen Talos in the centre (objective): defend it for 5 rounds and keep an engineer at the valve for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Niko's memory: a model standing at the valve knows no fear; once, it may release the steam jet — every model within 3" takes 1 Wound (itself included).
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; in the finale Talos starts with 2 extra Wounds.

### 4. The Arrival of the Sisters of Medea (1914)

Only the Colchian healers know the secret of the nail. Their ship is nearing the harbour in the storm.

- **Objective:** bring 3 healers (markers on the sea side of your edge) to the table centre.
- **Special rule:** the healers count as models (Mv 5, Wd 2, Ar 1); the enemy targets them.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown, and before the next battle every wounded model has recovered.

### 5. The Eye of Typhon (1914)

The nail has been replaced. Talos walks into the heart of the storm — into Typhon's eye.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: stop Typhon (the enemy's tier V) or hold the centre at the end.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Inside the eye (centre, 8") no wind blows.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

For the first time in forty-three years the storm died down. Talos stands on the shore with a new nail — forged by the Colchian sisters, fitted by Greek engineers. At the front they say the two now trust each other a little more.

camp:northern.en:
# The Wolf Winter — the Northern Union

> **Enemy:** Fenrir, the coils of Jörmungandr and the jötnar · **Hero:** Astrid · **Scenarios:** 5

In the North the winter grows longer every year. Fenrir's wolves besiege the fjord villages, and the old chain that holds him has been cut from the inside. Astrid, a veteran of Tyr's One-Handed, must forge a new chain — from impossible things.

## Sacrifice: Eirik the Horn-Keeper (1879)

**"Heimdall's Tower".** In the winter of 1879 Fenrir's pack took the fjord fortress at midnight, and the tower horn fell silent — the villages could no longer learn that the wolves were coming. Eirik, the old horn-keeper, climbed the tower, locked the door from the inside and blew until dawn while the wolves tore down the lower floors. Nine villages in the valley fled before morning. In the tower they found Eirik's horn, still warm.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Wolf Siege (1914)

A wolf pack besieges a fjord village; snow covers everything.

- **Objective:** defend the village centre (6") for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Snow: movement −1"; the enemy's tiers I–II are "wolves" (+2" movement).
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Impossible Things (1914)

The new chain needs the sound of a cat's footstep, the roots of a mountain and the breath of a fish — so the tale says. The smiths say these things are hidden in the war.

- **Objective:** 5 markers on the table; collect 3 and carry them to your edge.
- **Special rule:** picking up a marker replaces movement; a model carrying a marker has −2" movement.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Eirik's Horn (1914)

Heimdall's tower is besieged again. The horn lies where Eirik left it.

- **Objective:** take the tower (centre) and keep the model carrying the horn there for 3 rounds.
- **Special rule:** The horn: your models within 12" of it know no fear. Eirik's oath: if the horn-bearer falls, it gets one last activation, once.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; one warrior in the warband becomes "Horn-Keeper" (+1 Nerve).

### 4. Forging the Chain (1914)

The chain is in the forge, and the jötnar are coming down the mountain to destroy it.

- **Objective:** defend the forge (6" from your edge) for 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** the enemy takes a tier IV "Jötunn" outside the budget. A smith in the forge restores 1 Wound to one model each round.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown; the chain is ready.

### 5. Binding Fenrir (1914)

Fenrir is at the fjord's edge. The chain must be wrapped around him — by Astrid's hand, again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: land 3 "chain" hits on Fenrir (the enemy's tier V) (a net/chain, or a melee hit from a smith or the leader).
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. The fjord's coils: each round roll d10; on 1–2 a coil of Jörmungandr rises from the water and deals 1 Wound to a model near the edge.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

Fenrir is bound again — with a new chain, of impossible things. The winter is still long, but on Heimdall's tower the horn sounds again, every midnight, at Eirik's hour.

camp:celtic.en:
# Balor's Eye — the Celtic Isles

> **Enemy:** Balor and the Fomorians · **Hero:** Rowan · **Scenarios:** 5

On an island risen from the sea stands Balor's fortress, and his eye opens a little more every night. Lugh's Slingers are waiting for the bullet that will pierce the eye — but there is a traitor among them, and Rowan must find out who.

## Sacrifice: Siofra the Shield-Sewer (1893)

**"The Second Night of the Eye".** In 1893 Balor's eye opened for a single second, and the whole shore garrison burned — except those who stood behind a shield. The shield-sewer Siofra, who assembled sheets of lead and silver, carried the last great shield up the shore cliff and turned it toward the eye while the slingers fell back below, in its shadow. The shield held. Siofra did not. Lugh's Slingers still carry a fragment of that shield in their bullet pouches.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Fomorian Raid (1914)

Fomorian boats land on the shore at night and plunder the villages.

- **Objective:** sink 3 boats (objectives, 6 Wounds) before the raiders reach your edge.
- **Special rule:** the enemy enters from the water's edge. Currach sailors can board a boat.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Traitor Slinger (1914)

One of Lugh's Slingers is a Listener. He will give himself away during the battle.

- **Objective:** the enemy secretly picks one of your models — "the Listener". It is revealed when your leader comes within 6". Kill or capture it.
- **Special rule:** once, the Listener hands an activation over to the enemy.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown, and the mistrust die is not rolled in the next battle.

### 3. Siofra's Shield (1914)

The eye is opening again — and once again the shield must go up the cliff.

- **Objective:** carry the shield marker up the cliff (on the enemy's side) and keep it there for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** The eye: each round roll d10; on 1–3 every model not behind the shield takes 1 Wound. Once, the shield-bearer may "postpone" its death until the last round.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; in the next battle every model has a shield (+1 Armour against shooting).

### 4. The Three-Blow Bullet (1914)

Goibniu's smiths must forge the bullet with three blows — and the Fomorians are attacking the forge.

- **Objective:** 3 rounds: a smith at the forge (centre) — each round is one blow; the Fomorians must not stop it.
- **Special rule:** if the smith falls, the blow is lost; a new smith starts over.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.; in the finale one shot of the Lugh Colossus is at Power 8.

### 5. The Night of the Eye (1914)

Balor's fortress stops by the shore. The eye is opening — this time all the way.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: Balor (the enemy's tier V) — one bullet hit in the eye (a shot by a Giant-Hunter or the Lugh Colossus, 6+ to wound) kills him.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. The eye's strike: each round one of your models takes 2 Wounds.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The bullet pierced the eye, and Balor's fortress sank back into the sea. On the shore there now stands a monument of shield fragments — of Siofra's shield and of every shield that held for one second.

camp:finnish.en:
# The Stolen Sun — the Forests of Finland

> **Enemy:** Louhi and the river of Tuoni · **Hero:** Elina · **Scenarios:** 5

Louhi has hidden the sun and the moon in the mountain, and the forests of Finland are lit only by Ilmarinen's steam sun — forged, hung in the sky. But it is exactly that which keeps Louhi's gate open. Elina, a Singer of Väinämöinen, must find the real sun — and decide.

## Sacrifice: Aarne the Furnace-Keeper (1888)

**"The Cold Furnace".** In midwinter 1888 Louhi's ice host reached the steam sun's boiler — if the furnace went cold, the forests would freeze within a week. The furnace-keeper Aarne shovelled coal by hand all night while the ice warriors smashed the forge walls, and when the coal ran out he fed the fire his wooden leg and the door of his hut. The sun lit up in the morning. Aarne was found by the furnace, frozen, in the light of the embers.

## Scenarios

### 1. Twilight (1914)

Without the sun, day is twilight; the dead rise from the black river of Tuoni.

- **Objective:** 5 rounds: defend the village wells (3 objectives).
- **Special rule:** Twilight: visibility 18". Enemies within 6" of the Singers are at −1 in melee.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Forging the Steam Sun (1914)

The steam sun's boiler needs new plating, and the smiths go deep into the forest for iron.

- **Objective:** carry 2 iron markers to your edge.
- **Special rule:** Ilmarinen's forged men know no fear, but slow down without a song (−1").
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Aarne's Furnace (1914)

The ice host attacks the furnace again — the same forge that now bears Aarne's name.

- **Objective:** for 6 rounds the furnace (centre) must not go cold: each round one model must end its activation within 1" of it.
- **Special rule:** Aarne's fire: your models within 6" of the furnace do not suffer the frost (+1 Armour). If the furnace "goes cold" for even one round, the battle is lost.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; in the finale the steam sun is in effect for the whole battle.

### 4. The River of Tuoni (1914)

The road to the real sun crosses the river of the dead.

- **Objective:** get half your warband off the enemy's edge by crossing the river (the central strip).
- **Special rule:** The river: a model inside it takes a Nerve test each round — on a failure: 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Mountain of Pohjola (1914)

The sun is in the mountain's rock. Elina must open it with song — and then decide whether or not to put out the steam sun.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: a Singer sings at the rock gate (the enemy's edge) for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** The choice (before the battle): put out the steam sun — twilight, but the enemy cannot take tier V; or leave it — light, but Louhi comes with tier V.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience; two endings.

## Ending

The steam sun went out — it had never truly shone. The smiths forged a collar for Louhi, to chain her to the rock, and in the morning a dove landed on the forge window: the sun and the moon had come out of the mountain. Elina did not open the rock with song — Louhi opened it herself, out of fear. By the furnace now hangs an image of Aarne's wooden leg, and every winter they lay fresh coal beside it.

camp:britain.en:
# The War of the Fens — the Saxons

> **Enemy:** Grendel's mother and her spawn · **Hero:** Wilfred · **Scenarios:** 5

The fens wake at night, and the village halls where people sleep together are the first to fall. Wilfred, the only one left from the school of Beowulf's Heirs, knows where the lock is: beneath the mere, in the mother's hall — where Beowulf went down in the epic.

## Sacrifice: Oswin the Torch-Bearer (1890)

**"The Hall Door".** On a night in 1890 Grendel's mother came to the door of a hall where forty children slept — schoolchildren, pupils of Beowulf's Heirs. The hall-warden Oswin stood in the doorway with one torch and one sword and met the monster while the children ran out the back door onto the fen path. The door did not break until morning. One of the children was Wilfred.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Night of the Hall (1914)

Fen-spawn attack a village hall where people gather for the night.

- **Objective:** defend the hall (your edge) for 6 rounds; no enemy may get inside.
- **Special rule:** Night and fog: visibility 9".
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Fen March (1914)

The warband must cross the fen — to the mere.

- **Objective:** get half the warband off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** The fen: the whole table is difficult terrain (−2"), except for 2 paths; only the fen scouts know the paths exactly (+2" on a path).
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Oswin's Door (1914)

The mother attacks the hall again — the same hall. Now Wilfred stands in the doorway.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the hall door (a single point) must not break — one of your models must always stand within 1" of the door.
- **Special rule:** The torch: the door-warden gets +1 Melee and fire. Oswin's oath: the door-warden does not flee on a Morale test.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; Wilfred swears a new oath — the leader gets +1 Melee.

### 4. The Fortress-Ship (1914)

The fen fortress-ship is crawling toward the mere, and fen-spawn are clinging to its wheels.

- **Objective:** bring the fortress-ship (your tier IV or an objective) to the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** each round the spawn call 2 more from the water's edge.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. Beneath the Mere (1914)

Wilfred goes down beneath the mere, into the mother's hall. The warband must stay above.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: defend the shore of the mere; your leader is "underwater" (removed from the table) for 4 rounds and then returns.
- **Special rule:** tier V is allowed. When the leader returns, roll d10: 5+ — the mother is defeated (the enemy's tier V dies).
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The mother's hall is closed. Wilfred came up, sword in hand, and the first thing he did was carve Oswin's name into the hall door — exactly where he had stood.

camp:gaul.en:
# The River Monster — Gaul

> **Enemy:** the Tarasque and its spawn · **Hero:** Héloïse · **Scenarios:** 5

The Tarasque climbs the rivers and destroys the bridges. The Gauls are developing lightning technology together with Iberia — but the lock is in the first lightning rifles, and the two allies eye each other with suspicion. Héloïse, a liaison officer trained in Iberia, must find out the truth.

## Sacrifice: Gilles the Bridge-Keeper (1881)

**"The Stone Bridge".** In 1881 the Tarasque reached the town's last bridge while a column of refugees was on it. The bridge-keeper Gilles set off the charge laid in the bridge's middle arch when the monster was already on the arch — and did not run himself, because the fuse had to be held by hand. The bridge fell with the Tarasque. The refugees were already on the bank. The new bridge built in the same place is called Gilles's Bridge.

## Scenarios

### 1. Broken Bridges (1914)

The Tarasque's spawn are destroying the river crossings.

- **Objective:** control 3 fords (objectives) for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** a river across the middle of the table: crossing only at the fords; Belenos's Shield-Bearers know no fear at a ford.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Iberian Rifle (1914)

An Iberian engineer arrives with the drawings for the first lightning rifle. The Gauls must see him safely in.

- **Objective:** bring the engineer (marker/model) to your edge.
- **Special rule:** the enemy secretly decides whether or not the engineer is a Listener (revealed when he reaches your edge).
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown; if the engineer is a Listener — +1 more.

### 3. Gilles's Bridge (1914)

The Tarasque attacks a bridge again — Gilles's Bridge — and again there are people on it.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the bridge (centre) must not be destroyed, and you must bring 4 refugee markers across.
- **Special rule:** The bridge charge: once, the Tarasque Armour-Breakers may blow up the bridge with everyone on it (the enemy's tier IV dies).
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. Suspicion (1914)

The story of the lock has split the allies. Two detachments meet at the same ford.

- **Objective:** a battle against an ally (another light faction or Iberia); victory — when one side captures the other's leader.
- **Special rule:** no one dies: the fallen automatically recover.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown; defeat: the suspicion remains (−1 Renown).

### 5. The Wheel on the River (1914)

Taranis's Wheel goes into the river, toward the Tarasque's lair.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: kill the Tarasque (the enemy's tier V) or bring the Wheel to the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. A Tarasque wounded by lightning cannot regrow that round.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The Tarasque fell to the riverbed, and the Wheel's lightning lit the water until morning. Héloïse shook the Iberian engineer's hand on Gilles's Bridge — where the two nations had once already shared one man.

camp:italy.en:
# Vulcan's Son — Rome

> **Enemy:** Cacus and his fiery spawn · **Hero:** Giulia · **Scenarios:** 5

Cacus, Vulcan's fire-breathing son, is coming up out of the caves, and half the forges have stopped. Giulia, commander of Vulcan's Gunners, knows the lock is in the furnace: Vulcan's fire itself is feeding the gate.

## Sacrifice: Matteo the Gun-Boy (1897)

**"The Mouth of the Cave".** In 1897 Cacus sent fire from his cave down the town's main street, and a gunners' battery was left facing him without a charge. The gun-boy Matteo, sixteen years old, slung the last powder keg on his back and walked into the fire, up to the mouth of the cave. The explosion brought the mouth down, and Cacus could not come up for nine years. Every gun in the battery now carries a small metal plate: "For Matteo".

## Scenarios

### 1. The Fiery Night (1914)

Cacus's spawn are spreading fire through the town's streets.

- **Objective:** defend 3 water pumps (objectives) for 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Fire: each round 1 new fire marker; every model within 2" of one rolls d10, on 1–2 → a Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Caves (1914)

The front is in the caves: narrow, dark, hot.

- **Objective:** get 2 units off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** the table is 3 narrow tunnels (6" wide); shooting only along a tunnel.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. The Traitor Smiths (1914)

In one forge the furnace lights itself at night. Someone among the smiths has a key.

- **Objective:** capture 3 enemy smiths (its models).
- **Special rule:** smiths within 6" of the furnace get +1 Armour.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 4. Matteo's Mouth (1914)

The mouth of the cave that Matteo brought down is opening again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: collapse the mouth of the cave (on the enemy's side) with explosives — a gunner or sapper spends 1 round at the mouth.
- **Special rule:** Matteo's keg: one of your models may "carry the keg into the fire" — when it reaches the mouth, the explosion is automatic, and the model dies.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown; a plate for every gun — your gunners know no fear in the next battle.

### 5. The Hercules Colossus (1914)

The furnace must be put out — and Cacus guards it. The Hercules Colossus goes into the cave, just as in the myth.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: put out the furnace (centre) — your model next to it for 3 rounds; or kill Cacus (V).
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Fire does not harm Cacus.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The furnace went out, and with it — the gate. Vulcan's forges now work with another fire, lit by hand. And every morning the battery's boys polish the plates — even on the newest gun.

camp:polianitsy.en:
# Morana's Winter — the Northern Slavic Lands

> **Enemy:** Morana, Koschei the Deathless and the zmeys · **Hero:** Vasilisa · **Scenarios:** 5

Morana's winter has taken the men — they sleep in the villages, frozen, and the women fight: the polianitsy, the woman bogatyrs. Vasilisa knows the tale — Koschei's death is in a needle, the needle in an egg — and she knows the lock is there too.

## Sacrifice: Marfa the Bell-Ringer (1875)

**"The Zmey's Bridge".** In 1875 Zmey Gorynych came down on the bridge that joined two villages, while women, children and the sleeping men's sledges were on it. The bell-ringer Marfa wound the bridge bell's rope around her hand and rang with all her strength — the zmey turned toward the sound and fell on her, in the middle of the bridge, when the column was already across. The bell fell into the river along with the bridge. On winter nights the fishermen say the bell still rings beneath the ice.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Empty Village (1914)

The men sleep in the village. The winter's slaves are coming to take them.

- **Objective:** defend 4 houses (objectives) for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Snow: movement −1". A polianitsa (max. 1) knows no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Marfa's Bridge (1914)

The zmey is coming down on the bridge again — and there are sledges on the bridge.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: bring 4 sledges (markers) across the bridge.
- **Special rule:** Marfa's bell: one of your models may ring the bell — the enemy's tier V/IV must move toward it and attack it next round.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 3. The Oak (1914)

At the foot of the oak is a chest. Koschei's servants guard it.

- **Objective:** reach the oak (on the enemy's side) and carry the chest (marker) to your edge.
- **Special rule:** The oak's roots: difficult terrain within 6" of it.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 4. The Hare and the Duck (1914)

A hare runs out of the chest, a duck out of the hare. The tale repeats itself in battle too.

- **Objective:** 3 moving markers on the table (each round 6" in a d10 direction); catch 2.
- **Special rule:** catching a marker — a melee hit.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Needle (1914)

The needle is in Vasilisa's hand. If she breaks it, Koschei dies — but the men may never wake. That can only be learned at the end.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: Koschei (the enemy's tier V) — either break the needle (the leader stays still for 2 rounds) or defeat Koschei in melee.
- **Special rule:** The choice: break the needle — Koschei dies at once, but for the rest of the campaign everyone has −1 Nerve; fight — harder, but the men wake.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; two endings.

## Ending

The needle broke, and Koschei fell — as in the tale. But the men did not wake. In spring the women bound an effigy of Morana from straw and rags, carried it from village to village and threw it into the river — by the old custom. The ice shattered, and that morning the first man rose. The fishermen heard the bell clearly — for the last time.

camp:armenian.en:
# The Lakes of the Vishaps — the Armenian Highlands

> **Enemy:** the vishaps — monsters of the lakes and clouds · **Hero:** Nare · **Scenarios:** 5

The vishaps are swallowing the lakes, and the valleys are drying up. The old vishap stones — the stone guardians — still work, but one of them is false: "restored" in the Age of Sealing. Nare, a keeper of the aralezes, must find it among hundreds of real ones.

## Sacrifice: Aram the Stonecutter (1883)

**"The Drained Lake".** In the summer of 1883 a cloud vishap came down on a lake, and the lake shrank overnight. The stonecutter Aram knew that an old vishap stone lay fallen at the bottom of the lake — and that to raise it one man had to stay at the bottom, at the lever. He went down. The stone stood, the vishap rose into the sky with the water and vanished, and the lake came back — over Aram's head. The stone now bears his handprint, carved into the stone itself.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Dried-Up Valley (1914)

The valley's lake is drying up; vishap-spawn coil around the village springs.

- **Objective:** control 3 springs (objectives) for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** the Aralez-Keepers raise a fallen ally once (with 1 Wound).
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Road of Stones (1914)

The vishap stones line the valley road. Each one must be checked.

- **Objective:** 5 stone markers; your model spends 1 round at each — check 4.
- **Special rule:** the enemy secretly marks one stone as "false" — checking it summons spawn (2 models).
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Aram's Lake (1914)

The lake is shrinking again. At the bottom the stone has fallen again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the lake bottom (centre, 6") — your model at the lever for 3 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Aram's hand: the model at the lever gets +2 Nerve; if it falls before 3 rounds, a new one starts over.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. The Tork Colossus (1914)

The Tork Colossus comes down the mountain, and vishaps rise from the lakes in its path.

- **Objective:** get your tier IV or its escort off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** The cloud: winged spawn attack from above (2 enemy models with flight).
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The False Stone (1914)

The false stone has been found. The cloud vishap is waiting for it to be destroyed.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: destroy the false stone (on the enemy's side, 8 Wounds).
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Vahagn's Vishap-Slayers deal +1 damage to a vishap with fire.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The false stone shattered, and the cloud vishap broke apart into rain in the sky. The valleys are filling. Every morning now Nare's dog sits by Aram's stone, as if waiting for someone.

camp:oghuz.en:
# The Descent into the Underworld — the Lands of the Oghuz

> **Enemy:** Erlik, the divs and the spawn of Tepegöz · **Hero:** Aydın · **Scenarios:** 5

Erlik's well stands open in the middle of the Oghuz plain, and the divs come up at night. The lock is at the bottom of the underworld. In the tale the hero goes down the well and comes up on the Zümrüd bird — feeding the bird his own flesh on the way. Aydın, a Hunter of Basat, chooses this road.

## Sacrifice: Kamila the Well-Keeper (1878)

**"The Well Lid".** In 1878 a spawn of Tepegöz — a one-eyed giant — came up out of the well and headed for a camp full of people. The well-keeper Kamila rode her horse across the giant's path, loosed an arrow at its single eye and, when the giant fell to its knees, chained the well's iron lid to its leg. Both fell into the well. The lid closed over them. The Hunters of Basat leave a place in their quivers for Kamila's arrow — empty.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Night of the Divs (1914)

The divs come up out of the well and attack the camps.

- **Objective:** defend the camp's 3 tents (objectives) for 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Night: visibility 12". Hunters of Basat deal +1 damage to a one-eyed target.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Kamila's Lid (1914)

Rust has eaten the well lid; the giant's hand is coming up again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the lid (centre) — a sapper or the leader for 2 rounds; meanwhile a tier IV rises from the well (the enemy's, outside the budget).
- **Special rule:** Kamila's chain: one of your models may chain the tier IV (a melee hit) — both go down the well and leave the battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 3. The Div of the Underworld (1914)

At the bottom of the well stands the lord of the divs. The warband goes down with Aydın.

- **Objective:** kill the Div of the Underworld (the enemy's tier IV).
- **Special rule:** Darkness: visibility 6" — except for torch-bearers.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 4. The Lock (1914)

The lock is beneath Erlik's throne.

- **Objective:** carry the lock marker (the enemy's edge) to your edge.
- **Special rule:** the marker carrier has −2" movement; each round a div "calls" it — a Nerve test, on a failure: it moves toward the enemy.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Flight of the Zümrüd (1914)

The Zümrüd Colossus will carry Aydın up — and the price is flesh.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: bring the Zümrüd Colossus (your V) to the mouth of the well (your edge).
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides (Erlik's guardian). The price of flight: each round the Colossus moves, your leader takes 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

Aydın came up with the lock in his hand — lame, but alive. The well is still open, but the lock is above now. And in the hunters' quivers the empty place has grown by one: for Kamila, and for everyone who went down the well.

camp:nile.en:
# The Thirteenth Hour — the Lands of the Nile

> **Enemy:** Apep and his serpents · **Hero:** Nadia · **Scenarios:** 5

Every night the Sun-Boat goes out into the desert to meet Apep, and every morning it comes back — so far. Nadia, the boat's timekeeper, counts the hours of the night. And a night that should have twelve hours counts thirteen.

## Sacrifice: Samir the Helmsman (1889)

**"The Boat's Helm".** On a night in 1889 Apep's head struck the Sun-Boat's helm tower, and the boat sank into the sand — if it could not come out before morning, the sun could not rise. The helmsman Samir lashed himself to the helm with a chain and brought the boat out of the sand while Apep's serpents undermined his tower. The boat was coming back at dawn. Samir sat at the helm, eyes open, and the boat still held its course.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Sandstorm (1914)

Apep's sign: a storm comes from the desert, and with it — serpents.

- **Objective:** defend the oasis's 3 wells for 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Sand: visibility 12"; shooting into the wind at −1.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Gate of the First Hour (1914)

The gate of the night's first hour must be opened for the boat.

- **Objective:** 2 models at the gate marker (centre) for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Set's Spearmen deal +1 damage to tier IV.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Samir's Helm (1914)

The boat has sunk into the sand again, and Apep's head is coming down on its tower.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: defend the boat's tower (your edge); a helmsman at the helm for 4 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Samir's chain: the helmsman cannot leave the helm and knows no fear; when it falls, roll d10, 5+ — it stays with 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. The Extra Hour (1914)

There is a traitor on the boat — the one who sets the clock.

- **Objective:** the enemy secretly chooses one of your models as "the traitor"; Nadia (the leader) recognises it by coming within 3". Uncover and stop it before it reaches the clock marker.
- **Special rule:** until the traitor is revealed, it acts as your model.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Late Morning (1914)

The clock stops, and the boat must get through one night with the right hours — twelve instead of thirteen.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds = 8 hours of the night: the boat must hold out; at the end Apep (V) must not be within 6" of the boat.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. After round 8 the sun rises: the serpents die.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The sun rose on time — for the first time in forty-three years. The clock has stopped, and the boat counts the old way now: by voice, by the stars, by heart. And at the helm hangs Samir's chain — the new helmsman touches it every night before going out into the desert.

camp:yellow_river.en:
# The War of the Flood — the Lands of the Yellow River

> **Enemy:** Xiangliu and Gun · **Hero:** Lin · **Scenarios:** 5

Every year the Yellow River rises higher, and the dam — built of swelling earth — grows with it. The higher the dam, the more open the gate. Lin, a canal engineer, chooses the way of Yu the Great: the dam must be destroyed.

## Sacrifice: Wei the Canal-Man (1892)

**"The Burst Levee".** In 1892 one of Xiangliu's nine heads broke the levee, and the water poured down on the villages. The canal-man Wei knew that opening the old canal's sluice gate would send the water aside — but the gate opened by hand, from below, in the middle of the current. He went down. The gate opened, the water went into the old riverbed, and the villages were saved. Lin learned Wei's last drawing by heart as a child.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Flooded Plain (1914)

Water stands on the plain; Xiangliu's spawn attack the villages.

- **Objective:** 4 mounds (objectives), 6 rounds; your model on a mound — 1 point.
- **Special rule:** Water: difficult terrain between the mounds; the enemy's spawn get +2" in water.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Xiangliu's Blood (1914)

Xiangliu's blood poisons the earth — nothing grows there.

- **Objective:** kill one of Xiangliu's heads (the enemy's IV), but its blood must not be spilled on the fields (centre).
- **Special rule:** if the tier IV dies within 6" of the centre — the battle is lost.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Wei's Sluice Gate (1914)

The levee has broken again — exactly where it did in 1892.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the canal's sluice gate (on the enemy's side) — a canal-man or sapper for 2 rounds; then the water goes, and every enemy model within 6" of the gate takes 2 Wounds.
- **Special rule:** Wei's drawing: canal diggers move without penalty near the gate.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. The Nine Tripods (1914)

The monsters' weak points are drawn on the tripods.

- **Objective:** 5 tripod markers; collect 3 (a model who knows the tripods spends 1 round at each).
- **Special rule:** for each one collected, your warband deals +1 damage to tier IV/V in this battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. Blowing the Dam (1914)

The dam must be blown — and the Yinglong Colossus is ready to dig a new riverbed.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: lay 3 charges on the dam (the enemy's edge) and defend them to the end.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. After the blast (round 8) the table floods — anyone not standing on a mound takes 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The dam was blown, and the water went into the Yinglong's new riverbed. The plain was flooded for one summer — and then, for the first time in forty years, the river fell. Lin carved Wei's drawing at the head of the riverbed: "Give the water a way."

camp:japan_isles.en:
# The Oni's Treasure — the Islands of Japan

> **Enemy:** the oni and the Ōmukade · **Hero:** Hana · **Scenarios:** 5

After Momotarō, the oni's treasure never went back to the island — and it is exactly that which brought the gate home. The Ōmukade, a mountain-sized centipede, is wounded by two arrows. Hana, commander of Hidesato's Archers, will carry the treasure back — and loose the third arrow.

## Sacrifice: Kenta the Bridge-Keeper (1885)

**"The Centipede's Bridge".** In 1885 the Ōmukade crossed onto the city bridge, and under the bridge hundreds of refugees were in boats. The bridge-keeper Kenta packed the bridge's pillars with smiths' charges and lit the fuse himself, on the bridge, at the monster's feet — the fuse was too short to run. The bridge collapsed, and the river carried the Ōmukade out to sea. The boats were saved. Every year Hidesato's Archers shoot one arrow into the water where the bridge stood.

## Scenarios

### 1. Beneath the City (1914)

The oni walk the city's underground canals.

- **Objective:** defend 3 well-heads (objectives) for 5 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Canals: shooting max. 12". Karakuri warriors know no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Dog, Monkey, Pheasant (1914)

The tale's three scouts have scattered across the mountain.

- **Objective:** 3 scout markers in 3 corners of the mountain; gather them at your edge.
- **Special rule:** each scout gives one of your models +1 to something (speed / agility / sight) until the end of the battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Kenta's Bridge (1914)

The Ōmukade is crossing onto the bridge again. There are boats under the bridge again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: bring down the bridge (centre) before the Ōmukade (the enemy's IV) crosses — 3 charges on the pillars.
- **Special rule:** Kenta's fuse: one of your models may set off the last charge itself — the charge goes off automatically, the model dies.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. The Ōmukade's Mountain (1914)

The monster already carries two arrows. Now it is coming out of its nest in the mountain.

- **Objective:** 3 hits on the Ōmukade (IV) with your archers' or cannon's shooting.
- **Special rule:** Hidesato's arrow: once, one of your archers shoots at Power 7.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Oni's Island and the Third Arrow (1914)

The treasure is on the island. The Ōmukade and the oni surround it.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: place the treasure in the centre of the island (2 rounds) and kill the Ōmukade (V) with the third arrow.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. The third arrow: once, Hana (the leader) shoots at Power 9, damage 4.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The treasure stayed on the island, and the gate closed with it. The third arrow struck the Ōmukade in the head — as in the old story. That summer Hana shot two arrows into the water where the bridge had stood: one for Kenta, one for Momotarō, who first brought the treasure home.

camp:indian.en:
# The Twenty-Fifth Night — the Indian Peninsula

> **Enemy:** the bhutas — ghosts of the night · **Hero:** Anaya · **Scenarios:** 5

The bhutas have risen in their thousands from the old battlefields, and at night the villages live by lantern-light. Anaya, commander of the night patrol, is the only one the vetala speaks to. Twenty-four nights, twenty-four riddles — and on the twenty-fifth night she will learn the truth.

## Sacrifice: Ravi the Lantern-Keeper (1880)

**"The Line of Lanterns".** On a night in 1880 the wind blew out the line of lanterns that kept the bhutas from the village — eight of nine lanterns. The lantern-keeper Ravi took the last lit lantern and walked the line on foot, from one to the next, through the middle of the bhutas, and lit every one again. At the ninth lantern the cold brought him down. The line burned until morning. The night patrol still lights the lanterns starting from the right — in Ravi's direction.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Empty Village (1914)

The village is empty; bhutas walk the streets.

- **Objective:** search the village's 4 houses (markers) — bring the survivors to your edge.
- **Special rule:** Bhutas: enemy models cannot be harmed by shooting from beyond 12" without a torch.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Ravi's Lanterns (1914)

The line of lanterns is going out again — and the bhutas are nearing the village.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: 6 lanterns (on the table's centre line); each round roll d10 — on 1–3 one goes out. At the end 4+ must be lit.
- **Special rule:** Lighting a lantern: a model at the lantern, one activation. Ravi's oath: a lantern-lighter knows no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 3. The Elephant-Fortress (1914)

The Elephant-Fortress drives off the bhutas with its belly lanterns, but its lanterns must answer one another.

- **Objective:** get your tier IV or its escort off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** bhutas within 9" of the Elephant-Fortress are at −1 in melee.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 4. The Banyan Tree (1914)

The vetala hangs from the tree. Anaya must hoist it onto her shoulder and carry it away — in silence.

- **Objective:** the leader goes to the tree (the enemy's edge) and back to your edge.
- **Special rule:** Silence: the leader cannot shoot or give orders; each round a riddle (the opponent asks it) — a correct answer: +1" movement.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Twenty-Fifth Night (1914)

The vetala has spoken: the engineer is a Listener. The lock is at the foot of the tree.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the foot of the tree (centre) — take the lock marker and carry it to your edge; stop the traitor engineer (the enemy's leader).
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides (the Elephant-Fortress / the bhuta host). Bhutas within 6" of lantern-bearing models are weakened.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The lock is out, and the wave of bhutas has fallen back — to the old battlefields. The vetala still hangs from the tree and says it has one more riddle. Anaya will listen to it later. Tonight she is lighting the lanterns — from the right.

camp:west_african.en:
# Written and Spoken — the Lands of West Africa

> **Enemy:** Ninki Nanka and its spawn · **Hero:** Adjoa · **Scenarios:** 5

Ninki Nanka is coming up out of the swamps, and whoever looks at it directly dies. Every year the seal is bound with a song — now read from paper, "more accurately". Adjoa, a net engineer and the granddaughter of storytellers, compares her grandmother's spoken version with the paper. And one word does not match.

## Sacrifice: Kwame the Boatman (1886)

**"The Mirror Boat".** In 1886 Ninki Nanka came up the river toward the trading port, while the port's people were still at market. The boatman Kwame covered his boat with a great copper mirror, paddled out in front of the monster and let its reflection drift with the river's current — downstream, away from the town. Ninki Nanka chased the reflection until it reached the falls. Kwame went over the falls. The Mirror Riflemen engrave his name on their mirrors.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Fishing Village (1914)

Swamp-spawn attack a fishing village.

- **Objective:** 6 rounds: defend 3 boats (objectives).
- **Special rule:** Ninki Nanka's gaze: a model in direct view within 12" of the enemy's tier IV (without a mirror) takes a Nerve test — on a failure: 1 Wound.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Line of Mirrors (1914)

A line of mirrors must be set up in the swamp — to lure the monster astray.

- **Objective:** place 5 mirror markers in the swamp strip (mid-table) and keep 3 of them for 2 rounds.
- **Special rule:** the gaze has no effect within 6" of the Mirror Riflemen.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Kwame's Boat (1914)

Ninki Nanka is coming for the port again, and the market is full of people again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: "lead" the monster (the enemy's IV) off a side edge of the table — with the reflection marker.
- **Special rule:** The reflection: on its activation, your model with a mirror moves the reflection 6"; the tier IV always moves toward the reflection. Kwame's boat: one model may leave the table edge together with the reflection — the IV goes with it.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. Anansi's Cunning (1914)

Anansi beats the strong with wits. The warband must lure the monster's spawn into the net.

- **Objective:** "catch" 4 enemy models in the net strip (table centre) — with a net hit or a trap.
- **Special rule:** the Net-Weavers' net is in effect for the whole battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Seal-Song (1914)

Two versions are recited at the seal: the paper one and the spoken one. One is false — and Ninki Nanka can feel it.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: a storyteller (model) sings at the seal (centre) for 3 rounds.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Your models within 6" of the storyteller know no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The seal was bound with the spoken song. The paper copies were burned — and Adjoa sent a letter to every nation in the world: check your songs. In her letter she also wrote down Kwame's story — told by word of mouth, put on paper, once, so that it would not be lost.

camp:north_american.en:
# The Man and the Drill — the Forests of North America

> **Enemy:** the fearsome critters of the forest and the drill · **Hero:** Clara · **Scenarios:** 5

The monsters of the tall tales are coming out of the forest — hidebehinds, snallygasters — and underground the drill is digging, by itself, toward the gate. Clara's hammer gang must beat it, by hand — the way John Henry once did.

## Sacrifice: Samuel the Tunnel Lantern-Man (1876)

**"The Tunnel Collapse".** In 1876 a tunnel collapsed, and a snallygaster — a winged monster — came down at the tunnel mouth, where twenty workers were trapped. The tunnel lantern-man Samuel hung his lantern away from the mouth, drew the monster toward the forest with the light, and carried it before its eyes all night while the gang dug through the rubble. In the morning the tunnel was opened. They took Samuel's lantern down from a tree — still lit.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Tunnel Mouth (1914)

Creatures are coming up out of the drill's tunnel; the gang must hold the mouth.

- **Objective:** 6 rounds: the tunnel mouth (centre) — more models within 6".
- **Special rule:** the hammer gang gets +1 Power in melee underground.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. The Hidebehind Forest (1914)

Sentries you can never see behind your back hide in the forest.

- **Objective:** get half the warband off the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** Hidebehind: enemy models appear only from behind (within 6" behind one of your models).
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. Samuel's Lantern (1914)

The snallygaster is coming down at the tunnel mouth again. The gang is inside again.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: bring 4 worker markers out of the tunnel; lead the winged IV (the enemy's) away from the mouth.
- **Special rule:** The lantern: within 12" of a lantern-bearing model the tier IV always moves toward it. The lantern-bearer knows no fear.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 4. The Snallygaster's Night (1914)

An armoured train guards the railway.

- **Objective:** get the train (your IV or an objective) to the enemy's edge.
- **Special rule:** Rails: the train moves only along the centre line, +4".
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The Last Wall (1914)

Only one wall is left between the two tunnels. The gang and the drill dig at the same time.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds = a race: your gang breaks the wall with 8 "blows" (one model per activation), the drill — 1 per round. Whoever is first.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. In the tale the man won and died: on a victory your leader dies on a d10 roll of 1–3.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The gang beat the drill, and the drill jammed in the wall — in its own tunnel. Clara hung her hammer above the tunnel, beside Samuel's lantern.

camp:mexica.en:
# The New Fire — the People of the Valley of Mexico

> **Enemy:** the tzitzimime and the cold of Mictlan · **Hero:** Citlali · **Scenarios:** 5

On the Binding night of 1871 the fire was lit — but that fire was not warm. The tzitzimime descend at every eclipse, and Citlali, an astronomer-engineer, knows the terrible truth: the fire is old. Every fire in the whole valley must go out at once — and be lit again by hand, in the old way.

## Sacrifice: Mixtli the Runner (1882)

**"The Eclipse Torch".** At the eclipse of 1882 one section of the ring of torches went out, and the tzitzimime were descending through that gap — toward the children's house. The runner Mixtli took two torches and stood in the gap, arms spread, a living post of torches, until the other runners could bring new fire. The tzitzimime fell on him — and could not get through. When the ring was closed, the torches were still burning in his hands.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Dark Village (1914)

The fire in the village has gone out by itself; the cold of Mictlan stands in the streets.

- **Objective:** light 4 hearths (objectives) — a fire runner spends 1 round at each; 6 rounds.
- **Special rule:** Cold night: everyone beyond 6" of a lit hearth has −1 Nerve.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Mixtli's Ring (1914)

An eclipse. The ring has a gap again — in the same place.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: the ring of torches (8 markers in a circle) — at the end 6+ must be lit; no enemy may get inside.
- **Special rule:** the winged tzitzimime (the enemy) descend from above. Mixtli's memory: a model with a torch may "stand as a post" — it cannot move, but no flyer can descend within 3" of it.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 3. The Stairway of Mictlan (1914)

The secret lies below — on the nine steps of the chasm.

- **Objective:** 3 models of the warband to the enemy's edge (the bottom) and back.
- **Special rule:** The stairway: the table is 3 steps, and going down each one requires a Nerve test. The Mictlan Stair Raiders do not take the test.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 4. The Old Ember (1914)

An ember of Mictlan burns in the fire store. It must be taken out — by hand.

- **Objective:** take the fire store (on the enemy's side); carry the ember to your edge.
- **Special rule:** the ember carrier takes 1 Wound each round (cold) unless a torch-bearer stands within 3".
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 5. The New Fire (1914)

Every fire has gone out. In the dark the tzitzimime descend. The Quinametzin Colossus waits for the fire to be placed in its chest.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: survive in the dark; from round 5 the leader lights the new fire in the centre (2 rounds) and a runner carries it to the Colossus.
- **Special rule:** tier V on both sides. Before the fire, visibility 6"; after the fire — normal, and the tzitzimime are at −1 to everything.
- **Reward:** victory: the campaign is over; every survivor gets +2 experience.

## Ending

The new fire was lit — by hand, in the old way — and from the chest of the Quinametzin Colossus it lit up the whole valley. That fire was warm. The runners carried it to every house, and the first hearth they lit was Mixtli's house.

camp:amazon.en:
# The Meeting of the Waters — the Forests and Rivers of the Amazon

> **Enemy:** the Boiúna and the Mapinguari · **Hero:** Lucia · **Scenarios:** 5

Where the black and white waters meet, the line is moving — year by year, so slowly that no one notices. Lucia, a river pilot, has proved it: the measuring station is pumping black water into white, and when they are fully mixed, the Boiúna will wake completely.

## Sacrifice: Joaquim the Pilot (1889)

**"The Mad Pilot".** The old pilot Joaquim was already saying in 1889 that the line was moving. One night the Boiúna rose from the water and headed for a flotilla of fishing boats. Joaquim took his boat out in front of the monster, lantern lit, and led it along the line, toward deep water — away from the flotilla. The boat was found empty. Lucia found his measurements in her teacher's boat, under a plank — twenty-five years later.

## Scenarios

### 1. The Lost Boat (1914)

A boat has vanished on the river; Mapinguari spawn roam the bank.

- **Objective:** bring the boat's crew (3 markers on the bank) to your boat (your edge).
- **Special rule:** the river is half the table: only by boat or for models fast on rivers.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 2. Curupira's Tracks (1914)

The enemy must be led astray — with Curupira's cunning.

- **Objective:** lure 4 enemy models into the "wrong" corner of the table (with track markers).
- **Special rule:** False tracks: your scouts may place a track marker; an enemy model within 6" of it must move toward it.
- **Reward:** victory: +40 mch.

### 3. The Mapinguari's Roar (1914)

The Mapinguari comes out of the forest; its roar stops people in their tracks.

- **Objective:** kill the Mapinguari (the enemy's IV).
- **Special rule:** The roar: each round everyone within 12" of it takes a Nerve test — on a failure: it cannot move this round. The Mapinguari Hunters do not take the test.
- **Reward:** victory: +2 Renown.

### 4. Joaquim's Line (1914)

Lucia is measuring the line — exactly where Joaquim vanished. The Boiúna breathes deep.

- **Objective:** 8 rounds: 4 measuring points (on the river) — a boat at each; lead the Boiúna (IV) away from the boats.
- **Special rule:** Joaquim's lantern: within 12" of a lantern boat the tier IV moves toward it. A lantern boat that leaves the edge together with the monster removes both from the battle.
- **Reward:** victory: +3 Renown.

### 5. Sinking the Station (1914)

The station must be sunk — and the towns will be left in the dark again.
